what: 17 of Silver Creek's 22 buildings could not be entered — open-looking doors on sealed blockout lots
cause: Only 5 main-row lots (sheriff, hotel, store, church, saloon) were written enterable. The other 4 named lots (newspaper, doctor, blacksmith, livery) and all 14 side-street and cross-street lots defaulted to blockouts: no interior shell, and a solid full-footprint body collider over the whole building. Their doors hung visually OPEN (the street-lot builder always mates an open leaf), so the street read as walk-in storefronts while every one of them was a sealed box — the exact visual/physics mismatch the aperture contract names, at town scale.
fix: Every town lot with a door is now enterable: enterable: true on the 4 named lots and all 13 unnamed side/cross-street lots. interiors.js addShell builds each one a real interior (floor, wall lining, ceiling, doorway aligned with the facade door), the street-lot builder no longer lays the solid body collider over them, and their facade declarations came out of APERTURE_DECLARATIONS (a declaration would now fail state-runtime — the doors moved from facade to traversable). The elPaso shell houses, timber cabins, and the mission's sealed adobe block keep their declared states.
enterable-lot.png: a side-street lot's front door — previously sealed; now an open doorway onto a real interior (floor, lining, ceiling)
check: check-collision gained the paired assertions: a probe crossing a town building's back wall must be blocked, and a probe walking the church's front door centre line must pass. Full suite 23 PASS, exit 0. Live inventory: 47 town door apertures, all traversable; the only non-window blocked aperture left is the mission's declared facade.
